title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to chair 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council on 20th August 2026 in Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu
subtitle:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has envisioned a concept of 'TEAM BHARAT' for the nation, on basis of cooperative federalism, and the Zonal Councils are making significant contributions in this direction
With the spirit that strong states make a strong nation, the Zonal Councils provide a systematic mechanism and an important forum for dialogue and discussion on issues affecting two or more states or the Centre and the states
Under the leadership of PM Modi, the Zonal Councils meetings have become a strong platform for solutions through dialogue
body_text:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will chair the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council (SZC) on 20 th August 2026 in Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu. The Southern Zonal Council comprises the states of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Keralam, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, and the Union Territories of Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep.
Under Sections 15 to 22 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, five Zonal Councils, including the Southern Zonal Council, have been established. Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah, is the Chairman of the Southern Zonal Council, and the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Shri C. Joseph Vijay, is Vice-Chairman. The Chief Ministers of the member states serve as the Vice-Chairman of the Council by rotation. The 31st meeting is being organized by the Inter-State Council Secretariat, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, with the Government of Tamil Nadu as the host. It will be attended by the Chief Ministers/Lieutenant Governors/Administrators of the member states and Union Territories of the Southern region, along with two senior ministers from each state. The Chief Secretaries/Advisors and other senior officers of the State Governments, as well as senior officers of the Central Government, will also participate in the meeting.
The Zonal Council has also constituted a standing committee at the level of Chief Secretaries. Issues proposed by the states are submitted for discussion before the Zonal Council's standing committee and after deliberation there, the remaining issues are placed before the Zonal Council meeting for consideration.
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has envisioned 'TEAM BHARAT' for the nation, on the basis of cooperative federalism, and the Zonal Councils are making significant contributions in this direction. These councils function on the conviction that strong states build a strong nation. They provide a structured mechanism for dialogue and discussion on issues affecting two or more states—or the Centre and the states—thereby serving as a platform to foster mutual cooperation. Under the leadership of PM Modi, Zonal Council meetings have evolved into a powerful platform for finding solutions through dialogue.
The role of the Zonal Councils is advisory in nature. However, over the past few years, these Councils have proved to be an important factor in fostering healthy bond of mutual understanding and cooperation across various regions. With the cooperation of all State Governments, Central Ministries and Departments, a total of 69 meetings of the various Zonal Councils and their Standing Committees have been held in the last approximately 12 years, since June 2014 till now.
The Zonal Councils provide an excellent forum for resolving issues and disputes and making progress on them between the Centre and the member States/Union Territories, among the member States/Union Territories, and within the region. These Councils also discuss broad issues of national importance, which include the implementation of Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) for the speedy investigation and early disposal of cases of rape against women and children, as well as issues related to education, among others. In addition, various issues of common interest at the regional level are covered, such as issues related to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, issues concerning important projects related to water sharing, the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin), issues related to civil aviation, and several other issues.

enrichment.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah will chair the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council on 20 August 2026 in Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu. The Council comprises Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and the UTs of Puducherry, Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep, with Tamil Nadu CM as Vice-Chairman. The meeting, organised by the Inter-State Council Secretariat, will discuss issues like Fast Track Special Courts, Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act matters, water-sharing projects, PMAY-Gramin and civil aviation.
enrichment.context: Zonal Councils were established under Sections 15-22 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, to promote cooperative federalism by providing a statutory forum for dialogue between the Centre and states, and among neighbouring states, on matters of common interest such as inter-state disputes, border issues, economic and social planning, and law and order. There are five Zonal Councils (Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, Southern) plus the North Eastern Council, each chaired by the Union Home Minister with state Chief Ministers rotating as Vice-Chairman. Their role is advisory, distinguishing them from statutory or constitutional bodies with binding powers, but they have historically served as a mechanism to defuse inter-state friction, especially post-1956 reorganisation disputes (e.g., water sharing, boundary issues, Andhra Pradesh bifurcation matters). This release is primarily a routine announcement of an upcoming meeting, but it reiterates the legal basis and composition of Zonal Councils, which is a recurring factual topic for Prelims, and touches on themes of cooperative federalism relevant to Mains GS2.

prelims_questions.question: The Zonal Councils in India were established under which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: Zonal Councils were established under Sections 15 to 22 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, as stated in the release.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a member state of the Southern Zonal Council?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Southern Zonal Council comprises Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and certain UTs; Odisha belongs to the Eastern Zonal Council.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of Zonal Councils in promoting cooperative federalism in India. How effective have they been in resolving inter-state disputes given their advisory nature?

study_notes.reason: The release is largely a routine meeting announcement, but it reiterates well-defined, testable facts about Zonal Councils (legal basis, composition, chairmanship) that are a recurring Prelims topic; the analytical content (cooperative federalism) is thin and generic, not enough to sustain a Mains-heavy reading.

prelims.point: Zonal Councils were established under Sections 15 to 22 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, not the Constitution.
prelims.why_important: UPSC frequently tests the statutory (not constitutional) basis of Zonal Councils as a distractor against bodies like the Inter-State Council.

prelims.point: There are five Zonal Councils — Northern, Central, Eastern, Western and Southern — each chaired by the Union Home Minister, with a member state's Chief Minister as Vice-Chairman on rotation.
prelims.why_important: Composition and chairmanship pattern of Zonal Councils is a classic prelims fact tested via statement-based questions.

prelims.point: Southern Zonal Council comprises Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, and UTs of Puducherry, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, and Lakshadweep.
prelims.why_important: Aspirants must know regional composition to distinguish Southern Zonal Council from other zones in matching-type questions.

prelims.point: Zonal Councils have only an advisory role, distinguishing them from statutory bodies with binding powers.
prelims.why_important: A frequently tested distinction — advisory vs binding authority — helps eliminate wrong options in prelims questions on federal institutions.

mains.point: Zonal Councils serve as a structured, non-binding platform for cooperative federalism, resolving inter-state disputes such as water-sharing and boundary issues arising from the 1956 reorganisation.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on mechanisms strengthening Centre-state and inter-state cooperation, or on examining the effectiveness of advisory federal bodies.

mains.point: Despite being purely advisory with no enforcement power, Zonal Councils have sustained dialogue on contentious issues (e.g., Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act matters) over decades, showing the value of soft mechanisms in federal conflict resolution.
mains.theme: Limits and value of advisory federal institutions
mains.analytical_use: Can be used to critically examine why non-binding institutional mechanisms persist and matter in India's federal architecture despite lacking teeth.
